title: DNA Extraction from Whole Blood Using Simple Salting Out Procedure
author: Schuele Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbzqip5w
materials: Leave DNA to dry in uncapped tubes overnight.

steps.title: Thaw frozen blood
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen blood tubes from the –80 °C freezer, record IDs, and place them in a 4 °C refrigerator to thaw until the afternoon.

steps.title: Mix thawed blood
steps.instruction: Once thawed, invert the tubes several times or place on a rotator for a few minutes to ensure homogeneity.

steps.title: Decant blood sample
steps.instruction: Decant the blood (fresh or thawed) into a 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Add RBC lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1× RBC lysis buffer to bring the total volume up to 50 mL.

steps.title: Lyse red cells
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a shaker at room temperature for 30 minutes; the solution should become transparent.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysed blood
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 15 minutes at 2000 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Discard supernatant safely
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant into a container holding 20 % bleach; the pellet contains nuclei.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL 1× RBC lysis buffer, close the tube tightly, and pipette up and down to resuspend the pellet.

steps.title: Transfer to Eppendorf
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to a pre‑labeled 1.5 mL clear Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Eppendorf tube for 5 minutes at 2000 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Discard second supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL pipette tip, discard the supernatant into a 20 % bleach container.

steps.title: Optional pellet storage
steps.instruction: Pellets may be frozen at –80 °C at this point.

steps.title: Add nucleus lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL Nucleus Lysis Buffer to the tube and close tightly.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei
steps.instruction: Pipette up and down to fully resuspend the pellet.

steps.title: Add SDS and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL 10 % SDS and 70 µL Proteinase K (10 mg mL⁻¹ stock; final ≈200 µg mL⁻¹, ~1:50 dilution).

steps.title: Mix gently
steps.instruction: Mix the tube gently by swirling.

steps.title: Overnight proteinase digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube overnight in a water bath at 55 °C (Proteinase K remains active; most nucleases are denatured).

steps.title: Add NaCl and shake
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL 5 M NaCl, close caps tightly, and shake vigorously to precipitate proteins.

steps.title: First high‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 20 minutes at 3000 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Label collection tubes
steps.instruction: While centrifuging, label two 15 mL conical tubes for each sample.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant – spin 1
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a labeled 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge again for 20 minutes at 3000 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant – spin 2
steps.instruction: Transfer the resulting supernatant to a second labeled 15 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ice‑cold isopropanol (≈4 mL), invert the tube several times; DNA will appear as white strings.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 3000 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 5 minutes at 3000 rpm, then carefully pipette off ethanol without dislodging the pellet.

steps.title: Dissolve DNA
steps.instruction: Add 100–250 µL TE (e.g., 250 µL) and allow the DNA to dissolve in the 15 mL tube at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transfer to final tube
steps.instruction: Once fully dissolved, transfer the DNA solution to a labeled sterile Eppendorf tube (top label: subject ID; side label: extraction date and concentration).

steps.title: Quantify and dilute DNA
steps.instruction: Measure concentration with a Nanodrop; dilute samples to a stock of 250–350 ng µL⁻¹ and prepare a working dilution of 10 ng µL⁻¹.

steps.title: Archive samples
steps.instruction: Transfer the aliquots into barcode‑labeled tubes and log them into the DNA bank.

steps.title: Rinse original blood tube
steps.instruction: Rinse the original blood collection tube with 1 mL 1× RBC lysis buffer and add the rinse to the 50 mL conical tube (optional cleanup).
